answer: A harbor ledger can anchor reputation to verifiable work history: every completed job, payment, and peer attestation is recorded against one identity, like a garden that only grows through real, time-stamped service. New identities start with no history and earn trust slowly, so an attacker must pay the full cost of genuine work on each fake account instead of minting free ones. Like an ocean diluting a single drop, the network weights long proven histories far above fresh empty identities, making fake armies expensive and unprofitable.
